messages:
emily: Heads-up — launching a new Local Forensic Export feature for Private/VPC customers. Purpose: let approved customers pull a signed, redacted audit bundle from their on‑prem agent for regulatory or legal review. Rolling out next week; read details below and ping me for exceptions.

emily: TL;DR: canary Tue AM (10 tenants), broad Wed. Opt-in only: requires signed DPA addendum + admin confirmation. Agent v3.2+ required. Exports are encrypted, HSM/KMS-wrapped, and DLP rules apply.

emily: Customer-facing constraints: max 50GB per bundle, 1 export concurrently per tenant, rate-limited to 3 exports/hour. If bundle >50GB we provide chunked exports and guidance for local ingestion.

emily: Quick example (customer side API):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://private-console.redwood.example/api/v1/tenants/123/export" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"since":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z","include_telemetry":false,"redaction_profile":"pci-ssn"}'
```

emily: Note: `include_telemetry` defaults to false for privacy-first tenants. If customers request telemetry in the export, they must confirm purpose and sign the addendum.

emily: Internal impact summary:
- Security: signed artifact + audit trail; needs HSM policy tweak for export signing.
- Ops: agent upgrade job + monitoring of export queue.
- CS/SE: customer readiness checklist + consent flow.

emily: Action items for teams: please read and ack in-thread.

vikram: Ack. I'll add an agent pre-check to the upgrade job to require v3.2+. Also adding a kernel/memory check so big-export customers get a pre-warn.

alex: Question: does this change telemetry defaults? Will any additional telemetry be enabled if a customer opts-in for export?

emily: @alex no change to defaults. `include_telemetry` is explicit and false by default. If set true, we will only include telemetry types the customer explicitly listed and allowed by their contract. Full mapping in the runbook (link coming).

carla: Legal: we need the EULA/DPA addendum templates finalized before broad rollout. I uploaded a draft to /legal/templates/forensic-export-dpa.md — pls don't share externally until we finalize wording. We also need the consent checkbox flow documented for CS.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: canary export handlers scheduled 2026-04-07T09:00Z -> 2026-04-07T12:00Z. Auto-rollback at 09:30Z on failure threshold.

oncall: Add runbook notes: how to kill hung export jobs, how to refresh KMS credentials, and post-export validation steps (signature verification). Also add disk-space alert thresholds and temporary throttle knob.

sam: CS note — I'll run two 30min office hours for customers on Thurs/Mon to walk through the export process and consent paperwork. Please send me the final checklist.

jordan: Any SLA implications for Dedicated tenants running exports? Is there a latency or throughput SLO we should surface to customers?

emily: @jordan exports run in the background and are best‑effort for throughput; we will not change token‑generation or inference SLOs. We will publish export SLAs: expected delivery window (<= 24h for <10GB, <=72h for larger bundles), and we will offer expedited paths for emergency legal requests (requires signed expedited addendum).

emily: Security/infra owners — flagged for follow-up: update KMS policies, vet HSM signing, add monitoring alerts for export failure reasons (permission, size, corrupt artifact).

emily: Thanks all. If you need early access to a test tenant for demos, DM me. :party:
